Field.Label: Dashboards reads INDIGO_URL / INDIGO_API_KEY / DAHUA_USER / DAHUA_PASS from IndigoSecrets.py first. If you don't use IndigoSecrets.py, fill in the fallback fields below. All other options (legacy Sigen URL, cameras list, swap-out host, etc.) follow further down. The main-mosaic cameras and the per-room extras (doors, appliances, includes) are edited on the Settings page, not here.
Base URL of the Indigo REST API, e.g. http://127.0.0.1:8176. Fallback for IndigoSecrets.INDIGO_URL. Leave blank to use http://127.0.0.1:8176 — fill it in if your web server runs on another port.

Bearer API key for the Indigo REST API. Fallback for IndigoSecrets.INDIGO_API_KEY. NOTE: "secure" masks this field in the dialog but stores it in plain text in the plugin prefs file — prefer IndigoSecrets.py if you can.

Camera admin username + password (works for both Dahua and Hikvision). Fallbacks for IndigoSecrets.DAHUA_USER / DAHUA_PASS. Only needed if you have cameras configured. Stored in plain text in the prefs file (see the API-key note above).

Optional. URL of a legacy Sigenergy mini-dashboard (e.g. http://192.168.1.10:8179/). Used only by the "Open Sigenergy Battery Dashboard (legacy)" menu item; leave blank to disable the item. Read from IndigoSecrets.SIGEN_DASHBOARD_URL first; this field is a fallback.

Optional JSON list of camera objects. Each object needs host, name, vendor ("dahua" or "hikvision"). Read from IndigoSecrets.DASHBOARDS_CAMERAS first; this field is a fallback. Example: [{"host":"192.168.1.50","name":"Front Door","vendor":"dahua"},{"host":"192.168.1.51","name":"Drive","vendor":"hikvision"}]. Leave blank to disable the cameras grid and go2rtc (the :8177 proxy still runs, for /bootstrap only). All cams share DAHUA_USER / DAHUA_PASS from IndigoSecrets (despite the name, those creds also work for Hikvision).

Optional. Host of the camera that gets bumped from live MJPEG to a still snapshot when the user peeks at a tail-of-list camera. Defaults to the LAST entry in the Cameras list. Override only if a different cam is the better drop candidate.

Optional JSON list of action groups to hide from the Scenes page. Entries match an action group name, an action group ID, or "folder:Folder Name" to hide a whole folder. Read from IndigoSecrets.DASHBOARDS_HIDDEN_SCENES first; this field is a fallback. Example: ["Internal Reset", "folder:Maintenance"]

Region used by the Carbon page for grid-intensity + generation-mix data (the free Carbon Intensity API, no key needed — it covers Great Britain only). Pick the DNO region closest to you, or Off to hide the Carbon page and stop the lookups.
Auto-seed the API key to LAN browsers

When on (default), a browser on your LAN or Tailnet is handed the API key automatically on first visit, so it never has to be typed in. Turn this OFF if you run read-only guest devices and want the guest boundary strictly enforced — trusted devices then pair via the "Generate One-Time Setup Link" menu item instead. Off is more secure, on is more convenient.
Weather card extras (optional — IndigoSecrets OWM_API_KEY / LATITUDE / LONGITUDE win if present):
Adds sunset, today's high/low, UV and conditions to the hub's Weather card. Without these the card still works from your Ecowitt sensors alone.
System Health: battery device quiet after (hours):
Stale hours: a battery device that has not changed state for this long is listed as quiet on the System Health page. Low battery %: devices at or below this level are listed as low.
Leave blank to look for go2rtc on the PATH and then at ~/bin/go2rtc. Only needed if your copy lives somewhere else.

Where Indigo's SQL Logger writes its history. Leave this on SQLite unless you have deliberately pointed the SQL Logger at a PostgreSQL server. The Graphs, Timeline and Home Insights cards all read from here. Use "Test History Connection" in the Plugins menu after changing it.

These are read from IndigoSecrets.py first (HISTORY_PG_HOST, HISTORY_PG_PORT, HISTORY_PG_USER, HISTORY_PG_PASSWORD, HISTORY_PG_DATABASE); the fields below are the fallback for installs without that file. Access is read-only — the plugin never writes to the history database.

Indigo's reflector relays remote traffic through Indigo Domotics' own servers, and they pay for it. Camera pictures are far heavier than the reflector is meant for: nine snapshots a second from one page away from home is several gigabytes a day. If you reach this server another way when you are out — Tailscale, WireGuard, a VPN back to the house — turn this on and the dashboards will refuse the reflector entirely.

Field.Label: Log routine activity to the Indigo Event Log:

Leave this off and the routine narration - page and asset copies, config.js writes, and the camera poller, MJPEG proxy and go2rtc starting and stopping - is written at Debug, which normally means this plugin's own log file and not the Event Log. Ten to thirteen of them land on every restart, and the Event Log is shared with every other plugin. Tick this while you are setting the plugin up and they go to the Event Log as well. Warnings and errors always go to the Event Log either way, whichever setting you choose.

This box is not the only switch, so read it together with Log Level below. Log Level sets the lowest level this plugin puts in the Event Log: at Debug the narration goes there whether this box is ticked or not, and at Warning it stays out of the Event Log even when it is ticked. Everything written either way is in this plugin's own log file, at Logs / com.clives.indigoplugin.dashboards / plugin.log.

The lowest level that reaches the shared Indigo Event Log. It does not touch this plugin's own log file, which always keeps everything. Debug puts the routine narration above into the Event Log as well, so use it while you are chasing a problem and put it back to Info afterwards. Warnings and errors reach the Event Log whatever you pick here - Error behaves the same as Warning - because the estate's log watcher reads the Event Log and nothing else, and a fault it cannot see is a fault nobody is watching.
